label: Rosalie Iemhoff, Intuitionism in the…: Intuitionism: excluded middle is not a law of logic. p ∨ ¬p…
locator: §3.4, Weak counterexamples, 'the Goldbach conjecture is a weak counterexample to the principle of the excluded middle'
interpretation: Attribution reading: the Goldbach conjecture is a weak counterexample, since it is at present not known to be true or false, 'and thus we cannot assert ∀n A(n) ∨ ¬∀n A(n) intuitionistically, at least not at this moment. But the refutation of this statement ... is not true in intuitionism'. This is the withholding position: an undecided instance is not asserted, and the denial of every instance is refuted (the entry's 'the refutation of this statement is not true'). The statement does not say that no denial is asserted. The entry also notes that some classical laws (trichotomy on the reals) are not merely withheld but refuted with Brouwer's continuity axioms; that stronger position is not this statement's and is not recorded here.
